questions.question: Two coding agents use the same base model, but one finds files, runs tests, and retries on failures. Why can their outcomes differ?
options: Their scaffolding changes retrieval, verification, and failure containment
The model weights must have changed during every test run
A benchmark score depends solely on how long the prompt is
Only the programming language affects end-to-end reliability
questions.explanation: Retrieval, verification, and containment change how the same model finds files, detects mistakes, and limits damage, so scaffolding can change end-to-end outcomes. Model weights need not change for the scaffold to matter.

questions.question: What does SWE-bench Verified measure in the lesson's description?
options: Whether a model can run Python in any unrestricted shell
How quickly a model answers general knowledge questions
An agent's patch on a curated set of real issue tasks
A ranking of agent frameworks by license and feature count
questions.explanation: SWE-bench Verified presents real GitHub issues and checks whether an agent patch passes tests on a curated subset. It measures software-engineering task completion, not unrestricted shell access or general knowledge.

questions.question: What is the main tradeoff between JSON tool calls and CodeAct in this lesson?
options: JSON actions require a hardened sandbox; CodeAct is safe by default
JSON actions are easier to audit; CodeAct is more compositional with larger blast radius
JSON actions can edit many files; CodeAct stays limited to one file per action
JSON actions are free-form code; CodeAct is a typed function payload
questions.explanation: JSON calls are structured actions that can be validated independently; CodeAct composes several file edits into one Python action, increasing blast radius and sandbox requirements. Reversing these trade-offs misstates both execution surfaces.

questions.question: A team has many easy one- or two-line benchmark tasks but ships larger multi-file changes. What evaluation adjustment is most useful?
options: Use a harder subset that resembles the team's actual changes
Replace tests with a reviewer rating of code style
Keep only tasks that can be solved by changing one line
Choose whichever public leaderboard has the highest score
questions.explanation: If production work is multi-file and 10+ lines, evaluate on a comparable harder backlog rather than a benchmark whose easy tail includes many one-line fixes. Keeping only easy tasks increases distribution mismatch.

questions.question: A model can emit a multi-step Python program that reads, edits, and tests several files in one action. What condition should accompany this CodeAct design?
options: Allow unrestricted network and filesystem access to preserve flexibility
Skip verification because one action includes all the work
Treat the action as read-only because it is one message
Run the program in a hardened sandbox with measured permissions
questions.explanation: One CodeAct action can run an arbitrary Python program, so isolate filesystem, network, and process permissions. Treating a single message as read-only ignores the multiple consequential operations inside it.

questions.question: A production team asks which coding scaffold is best. What comparison does the lesson recommend?
options: Measure end-to-end reliability on a task distribution matching its work
Choose the framework whose prompt contains the most instructions
Pick the scaffold with the largest model name in the configuration
Use only the highest score on the easiest public benchmark
questions.explanation: Measure end-to-end reliability on tasks like the team’s actual work and under the scaffold it will deploy. A top score on the easiest public benchmark may not transfer to that distribution.
